intro: Two modules follow the AI-901 skills measured as of April 15, 2026: AI concepts and capabilities, and implementing AI solutions with Microsoft Foundry. Each combines a study guide, exam tips, key terms, visual slides, and a narrated lesson. Pair them with the free Microsoft Learn training and hands-on practice in the Foundry portal.

modules.title: Identify AI concepts and capabilities
modules.summary: Apply Microsoft's responsible AI principles, understand how generative models work and how to choose and configure them, and recognize common AI workloads: generative and agentic AI, text analysis, speech, vision, and information extraction.

guide.html: This domain is 40–45% of AI-901. It tests whether you can name the right kind of AI for a scenario, explain how generative models behave, and apply responsible AI principles. Questions are conceptual: you won't write code, but you need to recognize which capability fits a business need.

Microsoft's principles are fairness (similar people are treated similarly; test for bias across groups), reliability and safety (behaves as intended, including on unusual inputs; content filters and testing), privacy and security (protect personal data and the system), inclusiveness (works for people of all abilities and backgrounds), transparency (people understand that they're using AI and its limits), and accountability (people remain responsible for the system and its outcomes). Exam scenarios usually describe one concern and ask which principle it maps to.

Large language models are trained on huge amounts of text to predict the next token (a word or word piece). They understand meaning through embeddings, numeric vectors in which similar meanings sit close together, and the transformer architecture uses attention to weigh relationships among tokens. Output is generated one token at a time, so it can sound confident and still be wrong (a hallucination). Grounding the prompt in trusted data, as in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), reduces that risk.

Choose a model by capability (text, chat, reasoning, vision, image generation, speech, embeddings), quality, cost, latency, and context window. Configuration parameters include temperature (higher means more varied output, lower means more focused), top-p, max tokens (limits response length), and the system message that sets behavior. Deployment options trade cost and throughput, such as pay-as-you-go standard deployments or provisioned throughput for predictable heavy use.

Generative AI creates text, code, or images from prompts. Agentic AI combines a model with instructions and tools so it can take multi-step actions toward a goal. Text analysis includes keyword (key phrase) extraction, entity detection (people, places, organizations), sentiment analysis, language detection, and summarization. Speech covers speech recognition (speech to text) and speech synthesis (text to speech). Computer vision covers image analysis, tagging, captioning, object detection, and OCR, while image-generation models create new images. Information extraction pulls structured fields from documents, forms, images, audio, and video.

tips: Map each scenario to one responsible AI principle; the wording usually signals it.
Temperature controls randomness; max tokens controls length.
Grounding and RAG reduce hallucinations by supplying trusted data in the prompt.
Agents = model + instructions + tools, acting over multiple steps.
Speech recognition turns audio into text; speech synthesis turns text into audio.
terms: A unit of text (word or word piece) that models read and generate.
A numeric vector that represents meaning, so similar items are close together.
Fluent but incorrect or unsupported model output.
Supplying trusted source data to a model so answers are based on it.
Setting that makes output more random (higher) or more focused (lower).
An AI system that uses a model, instructions, and tools to complete tasks.
Detecting names of people, places, organizations, dates, and so on in text.

slides.title: AI concepts and capabilities
script: Welcome to the AI concepts module. This half of AI-901 is about recognizing which kind of AI fits a scenario, understanding how generative models behave, and applying responsible AI.
You won't write code here, but you will need to match business needs to capabilities.

slides.title: Six responsible AI principles
script: Microsoft's responsible AI principles are fairness, reliability and safety, privacy and security, inclusiveness, transparency, and accountability.
Exam questions describe one concern, such as a loan model treating groups differently, which is fairness, and ask you to name the principle.

Principle

slides.title: How generative models work
bullets: Fluent isn't the same as correct
script: Large language models predict the next token based on patterns learned in training. Embeddings represent meaning as vectors, and the transformer's attention relates tokens to one another.
Because output is generated, it can be confident and wrong. Grounding the prompt in trusted data reduces hallucinations.

slides.title: Choosing and configuring models
bullets: Pick by capability, cost, and speed
script: Choose a model for the job: chat, reasoning, vision, image generation, speech, or embeddings, balancing quality, cost, latency, and context window.
Temperature and top-p control how varied the output is, and max tokens limits length. The system message tells the model how to behave.

slides.title: Common AI workloads
script: Generative AI creates content, and agentic AI adds tools so the model can act over several steps. Text analysis finds key phrases, entities, sentiment, and summaries.
Speech recognition turns audio into text, and synthesis does the reverse. Computer vision analyzes images, and information extraction pulls fields from documents and media.

slides.title: Review: AI concepts
script: You've finished the AI concepts overview. Practice naming the responsible AI principle in a scenario and picking the right workload for a business need.
Then try the AI concepts question set.

modules.title: Implement AI solutions by using Microsoft Foundry
modules.summary: Use Microsoft Foundry to write prompts, deploy and test models, build chat clients and single-agent solutions, and add text, speech, vision, image generation, and Content Understanding extraction to lightweight apps.

guide.html: This domain is 55–60% of AI-901. It's hands-on: you should know what you do in the Microsoft Foundry portal and what a small app does with the Foundry SDK, for generative apps and agents, text and speech, vision and image generation, and information extraction.

A system prompt sets the assistant's role, tone, rules, and output format. User prompts carry each request. Good prompts are specific, give context and examples, and state the expected format. In the Foundry portal you pick a model from the catalog, deploy it, and test it in the playground, adjusting parameters like temperature and max tokens. A lightweight chat client uses the Foundry SDK with the project endpoint, authentication, and the deployment name, and sends the conversation history with each request so the model has context.

A single-agent solution combines a deployed model, instructions, and tools such as knowledge (files or search for grounding), code execution, or custom functions. You create and test the agent in the Foundry portal, then a client app starts a conversation, sends the user's messages to the agent, and reads its responses, including any tool results.

For text analysis, a deployed language model can extract key phrases, entities, and sentiment or summarize text based on your prompt, and Foundry Tools provide prebuilt language capabilities. Multimodal models accept audio and images as input, so an app can respond to a spoken prompt or describe a picture. Azure Speech in Foundry Tools provides speech to text and text to speech, including neural voices, for apps that listen and talk. Image-generation models create new images from text descriptions; describe subject, style, and composition clearly, and apply content safety.

Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools extracts structured information from documents and forms, images, audio, and video. You define an analyzer with the fields you want (such as invoice number, total, speaker, or topics), test it in the portal, then call it from a lightweight app that sends files and receives structured results (for example, JSON) to store or act on.

tips: Put role, rules, and format in the system prompt.
Test deployments in the playground before writing client code.
Agents need instructions plus tools; knowledge tools ground answers.
Multimodal models take images and audio directly as input.
Content Understanding analyzers define the fields to extract.
terms: Microsoft's platform for building, deploying, and managing AI apps and agents.
A hosted instance of a model your app calls by name.
Portal area for testing prompts and parameters on a deployment.
Instructions that set the model's role, rules, and output format.
Code library for calling models and agents from an app.
A model that accepts more than one input type, such as text, images, and audio.
Speech to text and text to speech capabilities in Foundry Tools.
Foundry Tools service that extracts structured data from documents, images, audio, and video.

slides.title: Building with Microsoft Foundry
script: Welcome to the Microsoft Foundry module, the larger half of AI-901. It covers what you do in the Foundry portal and what a small app does with the SDK.
You'll see generative chat apps, agents, speech, vision, image generation, and information extraction.

slides.title: Effective prompts
script: The system prompt sets the assistant's role, tone, limits, and output format. Each user prompt carries the request.
Strong prompts are specific, give context or examples, and say exactly what format to return.

head: Part
Example
rows: You are a helpful HR assistant

slides.title: Deploy and build a chat client
script: In the Foundry portal, pick a model from the catalog, deploy it, and try prompts in the playground while adjusting temperature and length.
A lightweight chat app uses the Foundry SDK with the project endpoint, credentials, and deployment name, and sends the conversation history so the model keeps context.

slides.title: Single-agent solutions
script: An agent combines a deployed model, instructions, and tools such as knowledge for grounding, code execution, or custom functions.
Build and test it in the portal. A client app starts a conversation, sends the user's message to the agent, and reads the response.

slides.title: Text and speech
bullets: Text analysis with models or tools
script: Apps can analyze text for key phrases, entities, sentiment, and summaries using a deployed model or Foundry Tools.
Multimodal models can respond to spoken prompts directly. Azure Speech in Foundry Tools adds speech to text and natural-sounding text to speech.

slides.title: Vision and image generation
script: A multimodal model can interpret an image in the prompt, such as describing a photo or reading a chart. Image-generation models create new visuals from text descriptions.
Describe the subject, style, and composition clearly, and rely on content filters to block harmful output.

slides.title: Content Understanding
script: Azure Content Understanding extracts structured information from documents and forms, images, audio, and video.
Define an analyzer with the fields you need, test it in the portal, then call it from an app and use the structured results.

slides.title: Review: Microsoft Foundry
script: You've finished the Microsoft Foundry overview. Practice describing the portal steps and what a small app sends and receives for each capability.
Then try the Microsoft Foundry question set.
